t:
(a) Physical Presence Rules.—Section 240A(b)(2)(B) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1229b(b)(2)(B)) is amended—
        (1) in the first sentence, by striking “(A)(i)(II)” and inserting “(A)(ii)”; and  
        (2) in the fourth sentence, by striking “subsection (b)(2)(B) of this section” and inserting “this subparagraph, subparagraph (A)(ii),”.   
    (b) Moral Character Rules.—Section 240A(b)(2)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1229b(b)(2)(C)) is amended by striking “(A)(i)(III)” and inserting “(A)(iii)”.  
    (c) Correction of Cross-Reference Error in Applying Good Moral Character.—
        (1) In general.—Section 101(f)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(f)(3)) is amended by striking “(9)(A)” and inserting “(10)(A)”.  
        (2) Effective date.—The amendment made by paragraph (1) shall be effective as if included in section 603(a)(1) of the Immigration Act of 1990 (Public Law 101–649; 104 Stat. 5082).

fable.w: The section consists solely of technical cross-reference corrections to the Immigration and Nationality Act concerning physical presence and good moral character rules, plus an effective date. A tempting reading is that it touches cancellation of removal, which involves individuals appearing before the government, but nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Immigration and Nationality Act, specifically correcting cross-references and citation errors. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. The changes are purely legislative corrections to statutory text.
qwen_block.s: Section 240A(b)(2)(B) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1229b(b)(2)(B)) is amended— (1) in the first sentence, by striking “(A)(i)(II)” and inserting “(A)(ii)”; and (2) in the fourth sentence, by striking “subsection (b)(2)(B) of this section” and inserting “this subparagraph, subparagraph (A)(ii),”.

opus.w: This section only makes technical changes: it corrects cross-references in sections 240A(b)(2) and 101(f)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act and sets an effective date. It creates no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The immigration-relief subject matter might look like participation, but an individual's eligibility for relief is an application for a benefit, and this text only changes citation numbers anyway.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The amended provisions cover cancellation of removal and "good moral character," so someone might read this as letting individuals take part in immigration decisions. That fails the definition. The section only fixes cross-references, and the underlying process is an individual applying for relief, which counts as an application for a benefit, not participation. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to statutory cross-references within the Immigration and Nationality Act. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. It also does not grant any outside party the right to sue or object to a federal decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 240A(b)(2)(B) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1229b(b)(2)(B)) is amended— (1) in the first sentence, by striking “(A)(i)(II)” and inserting “(A)(ii)”; and (2) in the fourth sentence, by striking “subsection (b)(2)(B) of this section” and inserting “this subparagraph, subparagraph (A)(ii),”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the Immigration and Nationality Act affects the rights of immigrants (outsiders), and thus involves participation. However, the definition of participation requires that the government *consult or coordinate* with outsiders *before* making a decision, or grant them a right to sue/object. This section merely corrects technical cross-references and statutory citations within existing laws. It does not establish a process for outsiders to participate in the decision-making process, nor does it grant new rights to sue or comment. It is a legislative correction, not a participatory mechanism.
